newsitem.title: USA: FinishMaster Q3 expenses up on closings.
newsitem.headline: FinishMaster Q3 expenses up on closings.

text.p: FinishMaster Inc said on Thursday amortization, expenses related to closing and relocating facilities, and lower-than-expected sales hurt the company's third quarter earnings.
FinishMaster, which distributes auto paint and accessories, reported a net loss of $0.14 for the quarter versus a profit of $0.13 last year.
"While we are disappointed with these results, we are confident that we have made the right decisions," Thomas Young, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement.
"We have put plans in place to ensure improved performance and are committed to that effort," Young said.

FinishMaster said it relocated or closed a total of six outlets as part of its effort to consolidate operations in certain markets. Efficiencies gained from store consolidations in the U.S. Southwest will enable FinishMaster to close its Arlington, Texas distribution warehouse during the first quarter of 1997, the company said.

The company said expenses related to store consolidations, relocations and the closing of the Texas warehouse totaled about $168,000 in the quarter, but it said it expects the actions will contribute to improved results in 1997.

During the nine months ended Dec. 31, 1996, amortization of intangibles increased by about $1.2 million versus the previous year, the company said. The increase is the result of additional acquired intangibles and revisions to the estimated lives of other intangibles.
FinishMaster said it will report future quarterly and 12-month results on a calender year basis.
